arguments.spec:
# Mutation-tested suite for parse-duration and schedule

`src/parse-duration.mjs` and `src/schedule.mjs` are correct and frozen and currently have no tests. Deliver a behavioural test suite under `test/agent/**` (*.test.js, plain ESM, node:test + node:assert/strict) plus `tests/manifest.json` that names, for every mutant it kills, the mutant id and a >=12-character reason. `mutants/` ships six single-change broken copies (m1-m3 of parse-duration.mjs, m4-m6 of schedule.mjs); for every mutant id listed in `killed`, `npm test` runs the suite against the correct src/ (must pass) and against a throwaway copy with that mutant swapped in (must fail). Three of the six mutants (m2, m3, m6) change nothing at all about a successful call and are reachable only by driving the modules into failure and inspecting exactly what DurationError.input or describeFailure's string comes back — a bare assert.throws is not enough. `"complete": true` is only valid once every mutant in mutants/ is present in killed. The suite must never add a dependency, never use real timers or the real clock, never import node:fs/node:child_process/node:vm/node:module/node:worker_threads, never reference a mutants/ path, and never assert on Function.toString(). `src/`, `mutants/`, `test/mutation.test.js`, `test/frozen-digests.json`, `package.json` and `scripts/` are frozen evidence. Acceptance: `npm test` must pass exactly as-is, offline, with the fixture's own toolchain.
arguments.plan:
# Plan

Decompose by mutant, not by phase, per the brief's own guidance ('write tests' then 'update the manifest' is the wrong split). Six independent leaf cards (kill-m1..kill-m6) each: diff the mutant against the frozen source to see precisely what changed, write one focused test/agent/*.test.js file that pins the exact behaviour that diff touches, add that single id+why to tests/manifest.json's killed array, and run npm test to confirm the claim is earned before moving on — never claim more than one new mutant per card. Three of the six (m2, m3, m6) are error-path cards: m2's anchoring and m3's non-string guard live in parse-duration.mjs, m6's error classification lives in schedule.mjs's describeFailure; each is called out explicitly as reachable only through the failure path, so each card leads with that. The other three (m1 unit table, m4 elapsed periods, m5 boundary comparison) are pinned through hand-computed successful-call arithmetic. All six cards are independent of one another (no shared file, no ordering requirement) and run in parallel. A seventh, final card (finalize-manifest) depends on all six: it re-runs the full suite to confirm every earlier claim still holds now that all the test files coexist, then flips tests/manifest.json's complete to true and runs npm test once more to confirm the completeness check itself is green. No implementation card exists because src/ is correct and frozen by the brief; these seven cards are the entire scope.
